text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on streaming gateway in eu-west-2. Customers: 3+ with degraded streams. Proactive paging to #incidents.

sara: paging in. I'm oncall.

liam: seeing increased tail latency for streaming connections. p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~ 2.8s -> 8.3s. Spikes correlate with interzone NAT path in eu-west2 -> eu-central.

priya: interesting, packet retransmits and TLS handshake timeouts showing in our egress NATs. dns latency also looks elevated for some subnets.

jay: any streaming stalls? IOPS on GPUs ok?

sara: yes stalls reported by customers — streaming chunks pause for several seconds then resume. Not GPU-bound. tcp retransmit and SYN retries up on nat-gw pool 7.

liam: dump from proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:03:11Z WARN stream-id=xx tail-latency=8321ms tls_handshake=timeout nat_path=nat-gw-7
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z WARN stream-id=yy retransmits=7 rtt=350ms
```

priya: running quick tcpdump on nat-gw-7, filter shows heavy retransmit bursts to interzone peer 10.40.8.1. Also seeing DNS NXDOMAIN retries with long timeouts.

jay: could be ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack stalls. Check conntrack counters and ephemeral port usage.

sara: conntrack count on nat-gw-7 = 785k (limit 786k). That's suspiciously close.

liam: that explains SYN retries — new connections failing to allocate conntrack entries -> retransmits -> long tail.

priya: reducing new connection churn is immediate mitigation. I'll enable connection pooling and enable our nat-ephemeral-boost on that AZ to increase ephemeral port range.

sara: do it. Also let's shift traffic for high-SLA customers to eu-west2-b which routes through nat-gw-3 (healthy). Can we add a routing override?

jay: creating a temporary routing policy: route customer routes -> eu-west2-b. Command:
```
rbctl route add --selector="tier:high-sla" --via nat-gw-3 --zone eu-west2-b --expires 60m
```

priya: nat-boost applied, conntrack limit temporarily increased to 1M on nat-gw-7. Watching counters.

ops-bot: NOTE: automated scaling attempted for nat-pool-7, but quota blocked. Manual adjustments applied by priya.

liam: after routing override, p99 for high-sla customers dropped from ~8s -> 480ms. Streaming stall reports for those customers cleared.

sara: communicate to customer success: short note to affected customers, say we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA. @marketing we should hold public comms until RCA.

priya: DNS TTL on our internal resolver had a spike; I'm flushing resolver caches in the affected VPCs. Command:
```
sudo systemctl restart dns-forwarder
```

jay: also noticed TLS handshake failure rates peaked — some backend peers were rate-limiting due to conntrack saturation.

liam: creating short-lived canary to redirect lower-priority traffic to fallback model variant with smaller context to reduce new connections per session.

sara: nice. For the oncall handoff: I'm going to hand to jay in 45m. If any customer escalations, page me.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 and packet retransmit metrics improving after routing override and conntrack increase. Continued monitoring 30m.

priya: still seeing sporadic drops on nat-gw-9 in eu-central. Opening a ticket with cloud provider for noisy egress path.

jay: action items: 1) provider ticket, 2) expand conntrack and ephemeral ranges as config default for nat pools, 3) add alert for conntrack > 80% - auto-scale nat pool, 4) update streaming docs with backpressure knobs.

sara: agreed. I'll write the handoff note and draft the customer impact summary.

liam: quick logs I'll paste to pagerduty incident later. For now saving captures:
- pcap: /var/tmp/2627-nat-surge.pcap
- proxy-logs: s3://redwood-ops/incident/2678901234/proxy.log

sara: final note before handoff: root cause likely conntrack saturation on nat-gw-7 causing connection failures -> retransmits -> TLS handshake spikes -> streaming tail latency. Mitigations applied: conntrack bumped, routing override for high-SLA, DNS flush, fallback routing/model for lower priority.

sara: handing to @jay now for next shift. moving to post-incident tracking channel.

jay: ack, I'm on. I'll coordinate RCA and provider engagement. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Metrics stabilized, customer reports normalized. Follow-up: RCA in product-ops repo and postmortem in /incidents/postmortems.
